newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka army launches offensive in north.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka army launches offensive in north.

text.p: The Sri Lankan army has launched a big offensive against Tamil rebels to open a supply route to a strategic government-held northern town, senior military officials said on Wednesday.

The three-pronged attack with air support was launched from Vavuniya, 220 km (140 miles) north of Colombo, on Tuesday, Sri Lanka's Independence Day, said military officials in the north of the country and in the capital Colombo.
So far, the army had encountered no resistance from the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Ealam (LTTE), said the officials, who declined to be identified.
The Defence Ministry had no comment.
The military officials told reporters the army's aim was to try to link the army-held frontline town of Vavuniya with Kilinochchi, 70 km (48 miles) to Vavuniya's north, and open a supply route.
The air force bombed rebel targets in the area surrounding Kilinochchi on Tuesday and Wednesday but there was no word on casualties.
The military officials had no other details but the newspaper Midweek Mirror said on Wednesday the offensive, involving thousands of government troops, was the biggest operation this year.

Kilinochchi, a town that fell to government forces last July, has been the focus of recent fighting between the two sides. Kilinochchi's only current supply route is a road linking it to the Jaffna peninsula in the northern tip of the Indian Ocean island.
The government can supply Jaffna, the LTTE's main stronghold in the country until last year, only by air or sea.
Early last month, the LTTE launched an offensive against government forces in the north in a failed effort to cut the Jaffna-Kilinochchi road.

In three days of fighting starting on January 9, the government said it lost 160 soldiers while the LTTE said 140 of its fighters, including 78 women, had been killed. Both sides claimed higher death tolls on the other side.

The LTTE has been waging a war for a separate Tamil homeland in the country's north and east since 1983. LTTE spokesmen in Paris and London were not immediately available for comment and the organisation has so far not issued a statement.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war but the LTTE says the toll is much higher.
